assessment_summary: In step 0006, the author claims that the components of the graph G=(V, M ∪ M') are either isolated vertices or cycles. This is incorrect. Because M and M' are perfect matchings, every vertex has exactly one incident edge in M and exactly one in M'. Thus, every vertex has degree 1 or 2 in G. The connected components of G are therefore either single edges (paths of length 1, where M and M' agree) or even cycles (where they differ). There are no isolated vertices in G, as that would imply a vertex with degree 0, which contradicts the definition of a perfect matching. The author likely confused the union M ∪ M' with the symmetric difference M ⊕ M' (where components are indeed isolated vertices and cycles).
